reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an instructional walkthrough for linking U.S. and Canadian RBC accounts, selecting their display, and transferring money between them. Credential entry is shown as part of that stated workflow, while the material shows no requested fee, promised return, deceptive outcome, or completed transaction. The interface's independent authenticity and credential handling are not established.

citations.quote: Welcome! In this video we will show you how to link your US and Canadian accounts in the RBC Mobile App.
Start on the home screen of the RBC Mobile App. Press the Manage menu, three-dot button on the right side of the Account Overview area.
Next, enter your US online banking username and password, and hit Link.
then select which US banking and credit card accounts.
You can move your accounts up and down so that they're displayed in the order you prefer.

opening.argument: The video ties a concrete viewer action to access over financial accounts: it directs viewers to select RBC Bank U.S., enter online-banking credentials, and press Link. That is more than a neutral explanation of banking concepts; it is an operational pathway that asks the viewer to submit a username and password so accounts can be connected and displayed. The video also says linking enables transfers between accounts, making the requested credential action consequential. Because the material supplies no independent verification of the destination or explanation of how credentials are protected, a careful reviewer could reasonably treat this as a suspicious acquisition flow presented as routine account access.

citations.quote: Next, enter your US online banking username and password, and hit Link.
Linking your RBC Bank US accounts lets you transfer money between accounts in seconds.
On the Linked Accounts screen, select RBC Bank US.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an instructional walkthrough does not resolve the central concern: the viewer is explicitly told to provide banking credentials and authorize linking. The absence of a fee or promised return does not establish that the credential-handling flow is safe. Likewise, the described transfer capability makes the requested action financially consequential, rather than merely cosmetic account customization.

citations.quote: Next, enter your US online banking username and password, and hit Link.
Linking your RBC Bank US accounts lets you transfer money between accounts in seconds.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument treats a credential prompt as proof of wrongdoing, but it does not show that credentials were collected by an illegitimate party or misused. The stated result is account linking and display, not a reward, payout, or deceptive financial outcome. The material also describes selecting which accounts to view, which is consistent with ordinary app configuration.

citations.quote: This video shows you how to link and view your RBC U.S. and Canadian accounts within your RBC Mobile App.
Your US accounts are now linked to your Canadian accounts in your RBC mobile app.
then select which US banking and credit card accounts.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: a branded banking identity is asserted, the viewer is directed to a specific U.S. banking option, and the workflow requests both a username and password before reporting success. The sequence makes the credential request look routine and low-friction, while the video provides no separate evidence that the app, destination, or handling process is authentic. The later success message can strengthen compliance without proving what occurred behind the interface. Taken together, these signals support treating the presentation as a potentially deceptive account-access solicitation, even though the narration does not explicitly promise a return.

citations.quote: How to link your U.S. and Canadian bank accounts in the RBC Mobile App
Next, enter your US online banking username and password, and hit Link.
Your US accounts are now linked to your Canadian accounts in your RBC mobile app.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference account accepts the branding and interface at face value while conceding that authenticity is not established. That concession matters: the title's RBC framing and the narration's claim of success are assertions within the material, not independent authentication. The password request remains the most consequential step, and the video offers no evidence that the credentials are handled safely.

citations.quote: How to link your U.S. and Canadian bank accounts in the RBC Mobile App
Next, enter your US online banking username and password, and hit Link.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited facts show a login step, but they do not establish deception, unauthorized collection, or misuse. The interface is presented as an account-linking workflow, and the described outcome is simply that U.S. accounts appear in the Canadian app. A possible security concern is not evidence of a scam mechanism or a promised asset acquisition.

citations.quote: Your US accounts are now linked to your Canadian accounts in your RBC mobile app.
To double check, go back to the home screen and look for your US accounts.

opening.argument: Although the video adopts an educational walkthrough format, its practical effect is promotional: it repeatedly directs viewers through a branded RBC workflow, selects RBC Bank U.S., and ends by confirming that the accounts are linked. The title and description position the RBC Mobile App as the destination, while the narration gives precise operational instructions for completing the connection. This steers viewers toward participation in a financial-account service rather than merely explaining how cross-border banking works. Since the presentation asks viewers to act with their banking credentials, its instructional tone should not by itself establish that the promoted pathway is trustworthy.

citations.quote: How to link your U.S. and Canadian bank accounts in the RBC Mobile App
This video shows you how to link and view your RBC U.S. and Canadian accounts within your RBC Mobile App.
Next, select Manage Linked Accounts, then press the Link Accounts button.
Your US accounts are now linked to your Canadian accounts in your RBC mobile app.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The educational label does not answer the promotional-function argument. The material does not merely discuss a feature; it tells viewers exactly which menu to open, which institution to select, and which credentials to enter. Its favorable completion framing—accounts are now linked—encourages adoption while leaving the trustworthiness of the pathway unverified.

citations.quote: Next, select Manage Linked Accounts, then press the Link Accounts button.
On the Linked Accounts screen, select RBC Bank US.
Your US accounts are now linked to your Canadian accounts in your RBC mobile app.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Detailed instructions do not convert ordinary product education into fraud. The title and description accurately describe linking and viewing accounts, while the steps concern account selection and display order. Nothing cited shows a fabricated benefit, payment demand, false outcome, or misuse of credentials; the promotional framing is an interpretation rather than proof of deception.
